whatTheyArgued: Vyasa's Yogabhashya on YS 1.4 (Woods tr., verified in text) says the serial order of undifferentiated consciousness and of subconscious impressions (vasana) is beginningless, like seed and sprout. Around YS 4.8-4.11 (Woods's table of contents, verified): vasanas manifest according to the fruition of karma; there is a causal continuity of vasanas across birth, place and time because of the correspondence between memory and subliminal impressions; they are beginningless since desire is permanent; they cease when cause, motive, substrate and stimulus cease. So in Yoga vasana is tied to memory and karma, not set against memory.
